slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you look
effortlessly confident in a room
Taking your time to choose a seat. Look around, pick a good spot, sit down calmly. Rushing to the nearest chair looks nervous. Choosing looks confident.
Introducing friends to new people. "Have you met Alex?" Making connections shows you're at ease and puts you at the centre of the room.
Laughing out loud when something's funny. A real laugh, not a polite smile. People who enjoy themselves openly always look comfortable.
Asking for what you need. "Could we turn the music down a bit?" A polite, simple request shows you feel at home, not like a guest who doesn't belong.
Always having something to add. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and knowing I'll never run out of things to say keeps me relaxed.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Never running out of things to say keeps me relaxed in any room.

slides.texte_overlay: Being fine standing alone for a minute. Sip your drink, look around, enjoy the room. Comfort with your own company is the clearest sign of confidence.
Leaving without a long explanation. "I'm heading off, great night everyone." A short, warm goodbye shows you're secure and happy in your own choices.
